question.text: Arbitrage opportunity exists when NIFTY spot is 22,000 and the one-month NIFTY future trades at 22,200. With a lot size of 50 and ignoring borrowing cost and taxes, what is the per-lot arbitrage profit if a PM buys in cash and sells futures to expiry?

explanation.text: The Logic: Spread = 22,200 − 22,000 = 200 points × 50 lot = Rs. 10,000 per lot, locked in irrespective of price direction. The Trap: Rs. 5,000 halves it; Rs. 12,000 uses wrong spread; Rs. 2,000 ignores lot size. Cross-Exam Context: VIII and XIII cover cash-futures arbitrage; XXI-B uses it as PM tool. Manager's Pro-Tip: In practice, impact cost + STT + financing easily eats a 50-bps spread — arbitrage windows in liquid indices are tiny.
